answers.label: Q1
answers.solution:
Write each decimal as a fraction: \(0.5 = \frac{5}{10}\), \(0.05 = \frac{5}{100}\), \(0.005 = \frac{5}{1000}\).

Product \(= \frac{5 \times 5 \times 5}{10 \times 100 \times 1000} = \frac{125}{1000000}\).

Divide top and bottom by 125: \(\frac{125}{1000000} = \frac{1}{8000}\).

So, \(0.5 \times 0.05 \times 0.005 = \frac{1}{8000}\).

answers.label: Q2
answers.solution:
Make the denominators the same. LCM of 3 and 4 is 12, but use 36 to leave room between the fractions:

\(\frac{2}{3} = \frac{24}{36}\) and \(\frac{3}{4} = \frac{27}{36}\).

The fractions between them include \(\frac{25}{36}\) and \(\frac{26}{36} = \frac{13}{18}\).

(Any two rational numbers between them are correct, for example \(\frac{17}{24}\), the mean of the two.)

So, two rational numbers between \(\frac{2}{3}\) and \(\frac{3}{4}\) are \(\frac{25}{36}\) and \(\frac{13}{18}\).

The first quotient digit is 5, so \(DE = 9 \times 5 = 45\): D = 4, E = 5.

\(4A - 45\) leaves 3, so \(4A = 48\): A = 8.

Bringing down B gives \(3F\), so F = B.

The remainder is 0, so \(GH = 3F = 9 \times C\). The only multiple of 9 between 30 and 39 is 36, so C = 4, G = 3, H = 6, and F = B = 6.

Check: \(486 \div 9 = 54\).

So, A = 8, B = 6, C = 4, D = 4, E = 5, F = 6, G = 3, H = 6.

answers.solution:
The values repeat in groups of three: A, D, G, J, M, ... = 2; B, E, H, K, N, ... = 3; C, F, I, L, O, ... = 4.

L is the 12th letter (12 is a multiple of 3), so L = 4.

I is the 9th letter (a multiple of 3), so I = 4.

N is the 14th letter (\(14 = 12 + 2\)), so N = 3.

E is the 5th letter (\(5 = 3 + 2\)), so E = 3.

Total \(= 4 + 4 + 3 + 3 = 14\).

So, the total for LINE is 14.

The question asks for the age of the student who left.

Total age of 33 students \(= 33 \times 13 = 429\) years.

Total age of the remaining 32 students \(= 32 \times 12\frac{15}{16} = 32 \times \frac{207}{16} = 414\) years.

Age of the student who left \(= 429 - 414 = 15\) years.

So, the student who left is 15 years old.

AOD is a straight line, so the angles on each side of it at O add up to \(180^\circ\).

Below AD: \(85^\circ + (2x + 15)^\circ = 180^\circ\), so \(2x = 80\) and \(x = 40\).

answers.label: Q10
answers.solution:
The pentagon is the rectangle ABDE with the triangle BCD cut out of it.

Area of rectangle ABDE \(= AB \times BD = 18 \times 10 = 180\) cm\(^2\).

In triangle BCD, \(\angle C = 90^\circ\), so by Pythagoras \(BC = \sqrt{10^2 - 8^2} = \sqrt{36} = 6\) cm.

Area of triangle BCD \(= \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 8 = 24\) cm\(^2\).

Area of the pentagon \(= 180 - 24 = 156\) cm\(^2\).

So, the area of ABCDE is 156 cm\(^2\).

So \(\left(\frac{2}{9}\right)^{-3} = \left(\frac{2}{9}\right)^{2m - 1}\).

So, \(m = -1\).

Prime factors: \(180 = 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 3 \times 5 = 2^2 \times 3^2 \times 5\).

The factors 2 and 3 are in pairs, but 5 is alone.

Multiply by 5: \(180 \times 5 = 900 = 30^2\).

So, the smallest number is 5.

answers.label: Q13
answers.solution:
Long division:

\(x^3 \div x^2 = x\). \(x(x^2 - 4x + 3) = x^3 - 4x^2 + 3x\). Subtract: \(-2x^2 + 8x - 6\).

\(-2x^2 \div x^2 = -2\). \(-2(x^2 - 4x + 3) = -2x^2 + 8x - 6\). Subtract: 0.

(Check by factors: \(x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 = (x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3)\) and \(x^2 - 4x + 3 = (x - 1)(x - 3)\).)

So, the quotient is \(x - 2\) and the remainder is 0.

Let my present age be x years.

Age after four years \(= x + 4\); age three years back \(= x - 3\).

Difference \(= (x + 4) - (x - 3) = 7\).

Present age \(= 4 \times 7 = 28\).

So, I am 28 years old.

answers.solution:
In triangle ABC, \(\angle A = 90^\circ\) and \(\angle C = 30^\circ\), so \(\angle B = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ\).

x, y and z are the exterior angles at A, B and C (each made with a side produced), so each equals \(180^\circ\) minus the interior angle there.

\(x = 180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ\)

\(y = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ\)

\(z = 180^\circ - 30^\circ = 150^\circ\)

\(x + y + z = 90^\circ + 120^\circ + 150^\circ = 360^\circ\) (the exterior angles of any triangle add up to \(360^\circ\)).

So, \(x + y + z = 360^\circ\).

answers.solution:
Note: the stem says the circles are drawn about the four corners (centres at the corners), but the figure shows four circles inside the square, one in each quarter. Both give the same numbers, as shown below. The question is read as asking for the space enclosed between the circles.

Circles about the corners: each touches its two neighbours, so radius \(= \frac{14}{2} = 7\) cm, and each covers a quarter circle of the square. Area covered \(= 4 \times \frac{1}{4} \pi r^2 = \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 154\) cm\(^2\).

(With the figure's four circles of radius 3.5 cm, area covered \(= 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 3.5 \times 3.5 = 154\) cm\(^2\), the same.)

Area of the square \(= 14 \times 14 = 196\) cm\(^2\).

Area of the square enclosed between the circles \(= 196 - 154 = 42\) cm\(^2\).

So, the required area is 42 cm\(^2\) (the circles themselves cover 154 cm\(^2\)).

Square: perimeter 176 cm, so side \(= \frac{176}{4} = 44\) cm and area \(= 44 \times 44 = 1936\) cm\(^2\).

Circle: circumference 176 cm, so \(2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r = 176\), giving \(r = 28\) cm.

Area of circle \(= \frac{22}{7} \times 28 \times 28 = 2464\) cm\(^2\).

\(2464 - 1936 = 528\) cm\(^2\).

So, the circle has more area, by 528 cm\(^2\).

Let the tens digit be a and the units digit be b. The number is \(10a + b\).

Sum of digits: \(a + b = 9\) ... (1)

\(10a + b - 63 = 10b + a\), so \(9a - 9b = 63\) and \(a - b = 7\) ... (2)

Add (1) and (2): \(2a = 16\), so \(a = 8\) and \(b = 1\).

Check: \(81 - 63 = 18\), the digits interchanged.

So, the number is 81.

Remove the innermost bracket first.

\(5r - 2(p - 2q + 3r) = 5r - 2p + 4q - 6r = -2p + 4q - r\)

Then \(-3\{-2p + 4q - r\} = 6p - 12q + 3r\).

Square bracket: \(2p - 3q + 6p - 12q + 3r = 8p - 15q + 3r\).

Finally: \(5q - [8p - 15q + 3r] = 5q - 8p + 15q - 3r\).

So, the expression simplifies to \(20q - 8p - 3r\).

answers.label: Q22
answers.finalAnswer: Construct triangle with AB = 6 cm, angle B = 60°, angle A = 45°; AC ≈ 5.4 cm; BC ≈ 4.4 cm
answers.solution:
Note: as printed, the question gives \(\angle CBA\) twice (\(60^\circ\) and \(45^\circ\)), which is impossible. It is read as \(\angle CBA = 60^\circ\) and \(\angle CAB = 45^\circ\).

Steps of construction:

1. Draw a line segment AB = 6 cm with a ruler.

2. At B, with the compass point on B, draw an arc cutting AB; from where it cuts, mark off the same radius along the arc and join B to that point and beyond. This ray makes \(\angle ABX = 60^\circ\).

3. At A, construct \(90^\circ\) (draw the perpendicular to AB at A), then bisect that right angle. The bisector makes \(\angle BAY = 45^\circ\).

4. The two rays meet at C. ABC is the required triangle (\(\angle C = 180^\circ - 60^\circ - 45^\circ = 75^\circ\)).

5. Measure AC and BC with the ruler.

Measured (and checked by calculation): \(AC \approx 5.4\) cm and \(BC \approx 4.4\) cm.

So, AC is about 5.4 cm and BC is about 4.4 cm. (If the angles are taken the other way round, \(\angle A = 60^\circ\) and \(\angle B = 45^\circ\), the two lengths swap.)

Volume of the wall \(= 600 \times 500 \times 50 = 15000000\) cm\(^3\) (since 6 m = 600 cm, 5 m = 500 cm, 0.5 m = 50 cm).

Cement and sand fill \(\frac{1}{20}\), so bricks fill \(\frac{19}{20}\) of the wall: \(\frac{19}{20} \times 15000000 = 14250000\) cm\(^3\).

Volume of one brick \(= 25 \times 12.5 \times 7.5 = 2343.75\) cm\(^3\).

Number of bricks \(= \frac{14250000}{2343.75} = 6080\).

So, 6080 bricks are needed.

answers.label: Q25
answers.solution:
Note: the numbers fit a growth over THREE years, not the two years from 1999 to 2001 as printed. \(\frac{92610}{80000} = \frac{9261}{8000} = \left(\frac{21}{20}\right)^3\), a perfect cube but not a perfect square. Taken strictly as 2 years, the rate would be about 7.6%, which cannot be found without a calculator. The intended answer is worked below.

Growth works like compound interest: \(92610 = 80000\left(1 + \frac{R}{100}\right)^3\).

\(\left(1 + \frac{R}{100}\right)^3 = \frac{9261}{8000} = \left(\frac{21}{20}\right)^3\).

\(1 + \frac{R}{100} = \frac{21}{20}\), so \(\frac{R}{100} = \frac{1}{20}\) and \(R = 5\).

So, the annual rate of growth is 5%.

Let the speed of the boat in still water be x km/hr.

Downstream speed \(= x + 3\); upstream speed \(= x - 3\).

The distance is the same both ways: \(5(x + 3) = 6(x - 3)\).

\(5x + 15 = 6x - 18\), so \(x = 33\).

Check: distance \(= 5 \times 36 = 180\) km and \(6 \times 30 = 180\) km.

So, the speed of the boat in still water is 33 km/hr.

answers.finalAnswer: Rs 23,375 (sold at a loss); Rs 19,125 (sold at a profit)
answers.solution:
Let the cost prices be Rs x (sold at 10% loss) and Rs y (sold at 10% profit). \(x + y = 42500\).

Selling prices are equal: \(\frac{90}{100}x = \frac{110}{100}y\), so \(9x = 11y\) and \(x : y = 11 : 9\).

\(x = 42500 \times \frac{11}{20} = 23375\) and \(y = 42500 \times \frac{9}{20} = 19125\).

Check: \(0.9 \times 23375 = 21037.50\) and \(1.1 \times 19125 = 21037.50\).

So, the cost prices are Rs 23,375 (the set sold at a loss) and Rs 19,125 (the set sold at a profit).

answers.label: Q29
answers.solution:
25% faster than 24 km/h \(= 24 \times \frac{125}{100} = 30\) km/h.

At 24 km/h he is 5 minutes late; at 30 km/h he is 4 minutes early. The difference in time is \(5 + 4 = 9\) minutes \(= \frac{9}{60} = \frac{3}{20}\) hour.

Let the distance be d km: \(\frac{d}{24} - \frac{d}{30} = \frac{3}{20}\).

\(\frac{5d - 4d}{120} = \frac{3}{20}\), so \(\frac{d}{120} = \frac{3}{20}\) and \(d = 18\).

Check: 18 km takes 45 min at 24 km/h and 36 min at 30 km/h, 9 minutes apart.

So, his office is 18 km away.

answers.label: Q30
answers.solution:
Take the external size as length 98 cm, breadth 84 cm, height 77 cm. The box is open at the top, so the wood (2 cm) is on four sides and the bottom only.

Internal length \(= 98 - 2 \times 2 = 94\) cm; internal breadth \(= 84 - 2 \times 2 = 80\) cm; internal height \(= 77 - 2 = 75\) cm.

External volume \(= 98 \times 84 \times 77 = 633864\) cm\(^3\).

Internal volume \(= 94 \times 80 \times 75 = 564000\) cm\(^3\).

Volume of wood \(= 633864 - 564000 = 69864\) cm\(^3\).

Weight \(= 69864 \times 0.8 = 55891.2\) g \(\approx 55.89\) kg.

So, the volume of wood is 69864 cm\(^3\) and the box weighs 55891.2 g (about 55.9 kg).
